elements.description: หลังคาเหล็กรีดลอน (corrugated metal sheet roofing), hatched vertically (parallel to the y/E-A axis) over the whole roofed plan; two 'SLOPE 6°' labels printed vertically down the two roof faces (one between grid1-2, one between grid2-3). CORRECTED THREE TIMES 2026-08 while extracting the elevations and sections (see warnings[] for all 3 reversals — this description is the final, current-best state): the roof is most likely a single, UNIFORM slope direction across the whole building width — LOW near gridA, HIGH near gridE, at ~6° pitch (possibly still built as two parallel mono-pitch planes over grid1-2 and grid2-3 respectively, per the roof plan's own two separate 'SLOPE 6°' labels and the fold line near grid2, but both sloping the SAME y-direction, not opposite as the 2nd correction guessed). This reading is supported by 3 sheets (_หน้า12_elevation4.json, _หน้า13_section1.json, _หน้า14_section2.json), against 1 outlier sheet (_หน้า10_elevation2.json/A-08, showing the opposite LOW-gridE/HIGH-gridA) that was re-verified 3 times and genuinely prints that way — most likely a real drafting inconsistency on sheet A-08 itself, not a misreading. Two curved swirl-arrow symbols near mid-plan (roughly grid1.5 and grid2.5, C-B row), likely roof drainage/water-flow direction markers, not confidently classified further.
elements.ridge_or_valley_lines: the line near grid2 is most likely a step/seam between two mono-pitch planes sloping the SAME y-direction (not a true ridge, and — per the 3rd correction — not a valley between opposite-sloping planes either; see warnings[])
